landing.title: CiteAura: AI Visibility & Generative Engine Optimization
landing.hero_copy: CiteAura traces AI answers, missing citations, and competitor gaps across a defined sample. Turn each finding into an assigned fix, acceptance check, and repeatable verification run.
landing.hero_title: Turn AI visibility gaps into engineering tickets.
landing.truth_title: Zero guesswork. Measure real AI visibility with rigorous data boundaries.
landing.truth_body: AI outputs vary by knowledge source. CiteAura strictly distinguishes between parametric model memory, web-grounded retrieval, and product-surface interaction. Unmeasured engines are reported honestly—empowering marketing teams with verifiable, multi-period trendlines.
landing.truth_engines_dd: Unified measurement across OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints with exact prompt tracing.
landing.truth_sampling_dd: Combine automated API sampling with manual product-surface checks in a single unified dashboard.
landing.truth_principle_dd: Unmeasured engines are never masked as 0%; every citation is grounded in reproducible prompts.
landing.workflow_title: From domain to verifiable delivery in 5 closed-loop steps
landing.workflow_body: Unify AI diagnosis, strategy, engineering tickets, verification runs, and client delivery into one standard pipeline.
landing.workflow_1_body: Crawl core site content, automatically map brand facts, competitor matrices, and target question sets.
landing.workflow_2_body: Inspect crawlability, structural semantics, extraction blocks, and authority signals across model matrices.
landing.workflow_3_body: Convert diagnosis into 13 standardized engineering tickets prioritized by Impact × Effort with clear acceptance criteria.
landing.workflow_4_body: Re-crawl deployed pages, compare AI sampling, and run verification explicitly when you are ready to evaluate progress.
landing.workflow_5_body: Generate executive audit decks, action matrices, ticket logs, comparisons, and assets with explicit readiness checks.
landing.product_title: Actionable evidence and engineering next steps on one unified screen.
landing.product_body: Every visibility score links directly to page-level gaps; every gap maps to engineering tickets and verification history.

landing.faq_1_q: Do API samples match what users see in the product UI?
landing.faq_1_a: Most APIs measure parametric model knowledge, not live product search. CiteAura clearly labels each engine as API · Model knowledge, API · Web-grounded retrieval, or Manual · Product surface for complete scientific integrity.
landing.faq_2_q: Must I bring my own model API keys (BYOK)?
landing.faq_2_a: BYOK is the most secure and cost-effective method. You only configure the engines you intend to use; others are honestly shown as unmeasured. Model APIs are extremely affordable (single audits typically cost ~$0.08–$0.15) with zero middleman markup.
landing.faq_3_q: Can CiteAura guarantee my brand will be ranked or mentioned by AI?
landing.faq_3_a: No. Any vendor promising guaranteed AI recommendations is untruthful. CiteAura provides rigorous diagnosis, standardized engineering tickets, and repeatable verification evidence to help teams improve visibility over time.
landing.faq_4_q: What is included in the 7-day free trial?
landing.faq_4_a: The 7-day free trial includes the trial workspace allocation: 3 projects, 2 sample runs per project, full reports, action tickets, and delivery packages with no credit card required.
landing.faq_5_q: Is CiteAura suitable for digital marketing agencies delivering to clients?
landing.faq_5_a: Absolutely. The Agency plan is tailored for agencies with 30 active projects, team role permissions, white-label client headers, and downloadable client-ready delivery packs.

docs.quickstart_p1: CiteAura is a Generative Engine Optimization platform that audits, measures, and improves brand citations, mentions, and visibility in generative AI engines, then closes the loop with engineering tickets and verification.
docs.quickstart_p2: This guide shows how to turn a public website into an evidence-based GEO workspace: crawl the site, record labeled AI answers, assign tickets, verify changes, and export a delivery pack.
docs.quickstart_callout: New projects start automatically. After you submit a website, the initial pipeline is queued. Keep the project open to follow its stages in the job telemetry panel; you do not need to find a separate start button.
docs.step_1_title: Step 1. Create a workspace and add a brand
docs.step_1_desc: Register at citeaura.com/app, then enter the canonical HTTPS URL for the brand. CiteAura creates the project and queues the initial crawl and analysis pipeline.
docs.step_2_desc: Open Diagnostics → Target Questions and Diagnostics → Brand Fact Library. Keep questions representative of real buyer intent and give material facts a source and verification date.
docs.step_3_desc: Open Settings → Model Keys (BYOK). Configure one or more built-in providers, or add an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Use Test to validate each saved key before sampling.
docs.step_4_title: Step 4. Run and inspect AI sampling
docs.step_4_desc: Choose Run AI Sample from Overview or Sample Matrix Now from Monitor. Review the exact prompt, raw answer, sampling mode, citations, and cohort before interpreting any score.
docs.step_5_desc: Prioritize evidence-backed tickets in Execution → Action Tickets, deploy the relevant assets, then run Verify Changes. Use Delivery → Client Delivery Packs to build the current handoff package.
docs.workflow_lead: The workspace follows a repeatable measurement and execution loop. Each view has a distinct role; use the evidence from one stage as the input to the next.
docs.stage_establish_desc: Crawl the canonical site and derive the initial question bank, facts, and audit evidence.
docs.stage_measure_desc: Record model answers for a versioned question set and classify each sampling mode.
docs.stage_diagnose_desc: Inspect technical extraction issues, observed framing, questions, and official facts.
docs.stage_execute_desc: Assign action tickets, edit generated assets, and prepare outreach or publishing drafts.
docs.stage_verify_desc: Re-crawl the site, evaluate acceptance checks, and reopen regressed tickets when required.
docs.stage_deliver_desc: Compile the latest audit, ticket, verification, comparison, and asset files into a ZIP package.
docs.workflow_callout: One active job per project: while a project job is queued or running, commands that start another job may remain disabled or return a conflict. Wait for completion or open the telemetry panel to inspect a failure.
docs.measurement_lead: CiteAura records observations from a defined question set. Results describe that sample cohort; they are not a guarantee of how every user, model version, region, or future answer will behave.
docs.mode_param_source: A provider API response without live retrieval.
docs.mode_param_interp: Measures parametric model knowledge for the submitted question.
docs.mode_ground_source: A provider API response with web retrieval enabled.
docs.mode_ground_interp: Can produce source URLs used in Citation Sources.
docs.mode_manual_source: A transcript captured from a consumer product interface.
docs.mode_manual_interp: Kept distinct from API observations because the product surface can behave differently.
docs.metric_mention_rate: Mention rate: the share of successful sampled answers in the current cohort that mention the configured brand identity.
docs.metric_avg_rank: Average rank: the observed recommendation position when a usable rank is present. An absent rank is not converted into a fabricated value.
docs.metric_sample_count: Sample count: the number of observations supporting the displayed metric.
docs.metric_citation_share: Citation share: the share of captured source URL mentions attributed to a domain within web-grounded samples.
docs.metric_unmeasured: Unmeasured: no qualifying observation is available. It does not mean zero visibility.
docs.byok_lead: CiteAura is 100% BYOK-native (Bring Your Own Key). You pay model providers directly at official API pricing with zero middleman markup.
docs.byok_security_p: Keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and injected only into runtime workers during active sampling runs.
docs.monitor_lead: Track multi-model recommendation trends, citation source distribution, and competitor mention share over time.
docs.diagnostics_lead: Audit site-wide technical blockers, crawlability barriers, schema entities, and verify canonical brand facts.
docs.execution_lead: 13 standardized engineering tickets prioritized by Impact × Effort, complete with code examples and acceptance criteria.
docs.llms_txt_lead: Publish machine-readable brand summaries and canonical documentation links formatted specifically for LLMs and AI crawlers.
docs.verify_lead: Re-crawl and sample after deployment to verify optimization impact, then export branded PDF decks and white-label ZIP packs.
docs.admin_lead: Manage team roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer), invite collaborators, configure OIDC SSO, and inspect activity logs.
docs.troubleshoot_lead: Monitor background pipeline stages, resolve crawler blockages, inspect API timeouts, and debug verification failures.
docs.question_cohorts_p: Changes to Target Questions create a different measurement input. Compare trends only when question scope, provider configuration, sampling mode, and market are sufficiently consistent. Raw answers and cohort labels are the audit trail behind aggregate metrics.
docs.callout_measurement_not_placement: Measurement is not placement. Adding an API key pays the provider for measurement calls. It does not alter model weights, buy recommendations, or guarantee citations.
docs.byok_lead_p: Bring Your Own Key routes measurement requests through your provider account, so provider usage and charges remain visible there. CiteAura currently exposes six built-in providers and supports custom OpenAI-compatible HTTPS endpoints.
docs.byok_openai_step1: Visit the official OpenAI Developer Platform (platform.openai.com/api-keys).
docs.byok_openai_step2: In the dashboard, click Create new secret key.
docs.byok_openai_step3: Select your organization or project, assign permissions, and copy the secret key.
docs.byok_openai_step4: In CiteAura, open Settings → Model Keys (BYOK) → OpenAI and paste the key.
docs.byok_claude_step2: Navigate to API Keys and click Create Key.
docs.byok_claude_step3: Name your key, copy the sk-ant-... token, and paste it into CiteAura under Settings → Model Keys (BYOK) → Anthropic.
docs.byok_google_step1: Visit the official Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com/apikey).
docs.byok_google_step2: Click Create API key and choose an existing or new Google Cloud Project.
docs.byok_google_step3: Copy the generated AIzaSy... key and paste it into CiteAura under Settings → Model Keys (BYOK) → Google.
docs.byok_custom_step1: Click Add Custom Provider in Model Keys.
docs.byok_custom_step2: Enter a provider name, the HTTPS API base URL, and the exact model ID. Do not append /chat/completions to the base URL.
docs.byok_custom_step3: Enter the API key and save. CiteAura tests the endpoint before retaining the configuration.
docs.byok_data_li1: Saved API keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and injected only while a provider call is running.
docs.byok_data_li2: API responses expose masked key identifiers, not the full secret.
docs.byok_data_li3: CiteAura does not use workspace content to train its own models. Provider processing, retention, and training controls remain subject to the selected provider account and policy.
docs.byok_data_li4: Delete a key from Model Keys to stop future calls through that credential.
docs.monitor_matrix_p1: The matrix groups the latest measured cohort by model provider. Use it to compare mention rate, average observed rank, sample count, sampling mode, and measurement status. Select Sample Matrix Now to queue a new cohort.
docs.monitor_matrix_p2: Open Raw AI Sample Answers & Citations before acting on an aggregate. The replay contains the exact question, answer, provider, mode, detected brand identity, and returned source URLs.
docs.monitor_citations_p1: This view counts only source URLs returned by web-enabled model samples. Parametric answers without URLs do not create citation evidence. Domain share is calculated within the captured cohort, not across the whole web.
docs.monitor_citations_p2: Use Draft Outreach when a cited third-party domain is relevant and there is a factual contribution worth proposing. Treat the list as observed evidence, not a directory placement guarantee.
docs.monitor_competitor_p: Add direct competitors to compare recommendation frequency in recorded answers. Keep the set small and commercially relevant. A competitor configured by a user is different from a competitor observed in model evidence; CiteAura preserves that distinction.
docs.diag_audit_p: Review crawlability, page roles, semantic structure, extraction blocks, and structured data. Page grades summarize applicable checks; skipped or non-applicable checks are shown separately. Use Re-run Audit after the public site changes.
docs.diag_gaps_p: Perception Gaps summarizes recurring descriptors found in recorded answers. It reflects sampled phrasing and does not independently decide whether a statement is factually correct. Compare it with the Brand Fact Library and raw answers.
docs.diag_questions_p: The question bank defines what the model matrix measures. Include real discovery, comparison, category, and problem-oriented questions. Avoid near-duplicates and prompts written only to force the brand name into an answer.
docs.diag_facts_p: Maintain official claims used by generated content and delivery assets. Prefer a source URL and verification date for material claims. The library is a controlled input; it does not override contrary evidence returned by a model.
docs.exec_tickets_li1: Prioritize by impact and effort, then open a ticket to review its rationale, target page, owner, requested update, and acceptance criteria.
docs.exec_tickets_li2: Assign an operational status only when it reflects the real implementation state.
docs.exec_tickets_li3: Attach decisions to the relevant question IDs so later verification remains explainable.
docs.exec_tickets_li4: Create a manual ticket when project evidence requires work outside the standard library.
docs.exec_workbench_p: Use the Workbench to compare recorded answers for a selected question and inspect the citations available to each response. It is an evidence review surface, not a second measurement engine.
docs.exec_assets_p: Generated project files can include machine-readable discovery content, structured data, deployment notes, and editable text assets. Review every claim and destination before saving or deploying an asset.
docs.exec_outreach_p: Outreach creates factual pitch drafts for relevant editors or authors. Publishing Destinations stores destination configuration and prepares drafts for editorial review. Neither workflow should be treated as automatic approval or guaranteed publication.
docs.llms_p1: /llms.txt is an emerging machine-readable discovery convention, not a universal indexing standard. It can present official facts and links in a concise Markdown file, but support varies by crawler and provider.
docs.llms_step1: Review the generated file in Execution → Assets & Templates.
docs.llms_step2: Remove unsupported claims and confirm every URL is canonical and public.
docs.llms_step3: Deploy it at https://example.com/llms.txt with a successful text response.
docs.llms_step4: Re-crawl and verify availability. Do not interpret availability as proof that a model consumed it.
docs.verify_cl_p: Run verification after public changes have been deployed. Verification re-crawls the site and evaluates ticket acceptance checks against the latest audit and metrics artifacts. It records pass, fail, and reopened states; it does not convert an implementation claim into a pass without supporting evidence.
docs.verify_step1: Deploy the selected ticket changes to the canonical public site.
docs.verify_step2: Open Execution → Closed-Loop Verify and choose Run Verification.
docs.verify_step3: Inspect the verification history and failed acceptance checks.
docs.verify_step4: Run a separate AI sample when you also need a fresh model-answer cohort.
docs.verify_packs_p1: Open Delivery → Client Delivery Packs and choose Build New Delivery Pack. The job compiles the current audit, action matrix, ticket log, comparison and verification evidence, and implementation assets into a downloadable ZIP.
docs.verify_packs_p2: Configure Delivery → White-Label Branding before building the pack when it needs an agency name, logo, or confidentiality notice. Rebuild the pack after material workspace changes; an older ZIP is a point-in-time artifact.
g1.h1: How to Measure ChatGPT Brand Mentions
g1.lead: You cannot treat one ChatGPT reply as a measurement. To measure if ChatGPT mentions your brand, fix a question set, record each raw answer, and mark whether the brand name or official domain appears. Repeat the same questions later. CiteAura stores those traces with a sampling-mode label so a mention rate is tied to a defined cohort, not a screenshot.
g1.byline: By CiteAura Editorial Team · Evidence and documentation
g1.sec1_p1: A mention is a usable string match in the recorded answer: the brand name you configured, a clear alias, or the official domain. A source URL is a different signal. ChatGPT only returns citations in some product or retrieval modes, so “no link” is not the same as “no mention.”
g1.sec1_p2: Do not convert a missing rank into a fake rank. Many answers name a brand without ordering a list. Record rank only when the answer actually ranks options.
g1.sec2_h2: How to measure it without guessing
g1.sec2_li1: Write 10–20 questions a buyer would ask. Include category, comparison, and problem prompts. Avoid “tell me about [your brand].”
g1.sec2_li2: Ask the same questions in the same market and language.
g1.sec2_li3: Save the question, raw answer, date, and whether you used the ChatGPT product UI or an API.
g1.sec2_li4: Mark each successful answer as mentioned or not mentioned.
g1.sec2_li5: Compute mention rate as mentioned ÷ successful answers in that cohort.
g1.sec2_li6: Repeat later with the same questions before you call the change a trend.
g1.sec2_p: A cohort is the unit of measurement. If you change the questions, the providers, or the product surface, you started a new series.
g1.sec3_h2: API knowledge is not the ChatGPT product UI
g1.sec3_p: Most developer APIs measure parametric model knowledge. The consumer ChatGPT app can retrieve the web, apply memory, or use a different system prompt. Mixing those answers into one percentage hides the method.
g1.sec3_callout: Label every sample. An unlabeled “ChatGPT said this” log is not comparable next month.
g1.sec4_p1: In the workspace you keep a target question bank, run a sample, and inspect the raw answer next to the aggregate. Mention rate, sample count, and sampling mode stay attached to that cohort. Unmeasured providers stay unmeasured; they are not shown as 0%.
g1.sec5_h2: A mention rate is not a ranking promise
g1.sec5_p1: Answers vary by model version, region, and retrieval path. A higher mention rate on a fixed question set is evidence about that sample. It does not guarantee that ChatGPT will mention or rank the brand for every user.
g1.cta_p: Set up a domain, keep the question set stable, and review labeled ChatGPT samples in one workspace.
g2.h1: Why ChatGPT Does Not Mention Your Brand
g2.lead: If ChatGPT ignores your brand in answers where competitors appear, do not assume an algorithm penalty. The cause is usually simpler: crawler access blocks, weak entity extraction, missing schema markup, or thin third-party citations. Follow these four diagnostic checks to find the real barrier.
